title: On making a life that leaves room for all of you
summary: Why a creative practice doesn’t need to become smaller in order to become clear.
body:
This is a sample opening for your first journal post. Replace it with the thought you cannot stop turning over—the one that feels worth leaving somewhere other people can find it.

## You are allowed to contain multitudes

The pressure to choose one identity can make a curious person feel scattered. But the throughline may not be a medium. It may be the way you notice, the questions you ask, or the kind of feeling you want to leave behind.

A photograph, a Minecraft world, a printed object, and a brand can all come from the same pair of hands. Clarity is not always about subtraction. Sometimes it is about naming the thing that connects it all.

## Keep a record

The archive is not proof that every idea worked. It is evidence that you kept paying attention. Over time, the record becomes its own kind of self-portrait.
